blocks.orig: Rubondo Island national park has a size of 240 km². It is only one of two Tanzanian national parks located on an island in Lake Victoria, the world’s second-largest lake. It is located in the southwest corner of the lake. Rubondo became a game reserve in 1965, to provide a sanctuary for animals. Tanzania gazetted Rubondo in 1977 as a national park. It is uninhabited and consequently 90% of the island remains forest today. With nine smaller islands under its wing, Rubondo also protects precious fish breeding grounds.
blocks.html: Covering 240 km², Rubondo Island national park is one of just two Tanzanian national parks set on an island in Lake Victoria, the second-largest lake on earth. You will find it in the lake's southwest corner. In 1965 Rubondo was made a game reserve so that animals would have a safe haven, and in 1977 Tanzania gazetted it as a national park. Nobody lives on the island, which is why 90% of it is still forest today. Rubondo also looks after nine smaller islands and with them some valuable fish breeding grounds.

blocks.orig: Rubondo Island offers many deserted sandy beaches that border directly on the forest. Here you will find bushbucks, which move smoothly and silently through the labyrinth of tamarind, palm trees and sycamore figs. The shaggy-coated aquatic sitatunga, which lives by the water, with its distinct webbed feet, can be observed particularly well here. Savory tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) are the main food of the yellow-spotted otters that hunt around the island’s rocky bays, while the predatory Nile perch, weighing up to 100 kg, is a tempting challenge for hungry fishermen in Rubondo Island national park.
blocks.html: On Rubondo Island, many empty sandy beaches run straight up to the edge of the forest. This is where you will spot bushbucks slipping quietly and gracefully through a maze of tamarind, palm trees and sycamore figs. The water-loving sitatunga, with its shaggy coat and unmistakable webbed feet, is unusually easy to watch here. Tasty tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) form the main diet of the yellow-spotted otters that hunt in the island's rocky bays, while the predatory Nile perch, which can weigh up to 100 kg, offers a tempting challenge to keen anglers in Rubondo Island national park.

blocks.orig: Wild jasmine and numerous colorful orchid species grow in the forest, from which a mysterious potpourri of scents flows. 90% percent of the park is considered to be forest. There are also open grasslands and papyrus groves by the lake. Indigenous wild animals such as hippos, crocodiles, vervet monkeys, genets, dikdiks and mongooses share their habitat with the chimpanzees, black and white colobus monkeys, elephants and giraffes that have subsequently settled here. The remoteness of this national park allows them to develop freely.
blocks.html: The forest is home to wild jasmine and a great many colourful orchid species, and a mysterious blend of scents drifts out of it. Forest makes up 90% percent of the park, but there are open grasslands too, and papyrus groves along the lakeshore. Native animals such as hippos, crocodiles, vervet monkeys, genets, dikdiks and mongooses live side by side with the chimpanzees, black and white colobus monkeys, elephants and giraffes that were introduced later. Because the park is so remote, they can thrive undisturbed.

blocks.orig: The Rubondo National Park: A bird watcher’s paradise
blocks.html: Rubondo National Park: a haven for bird watchers

blocks.orig: Birds are omnipresent on the island and make the Rubondo National Park an insider tip for ornithologists. More than 400 species have been registered over the years. Flocks of African gray parrots, which were once released on the island, flutter around excitedly and chirp in different tones. Herons, storks and spoonbills breed in large numbers in the swampy bank areas. Thousands of Eurasian migratory birds join them every year.
blocks.html: Birds are everywhere on the island, which makes Rubondo National Park a well-kept secret among ornithologists. Over the years more than 400 species have been recorded. Flocks of African grey parrots, released on the island long ago, flit about excitedly and call in a range of tones. In the marshy areas along the shore, herons, storks and spoonbills nest in great numbers, and every year thousands of migratory birds from Eurasia arrive to join them.

blocks.orig: The Rubondo Island national park is located on an island in the middle of Lake Victoria, the second largest lake in the world. The island is uninhabited and 90% of the island is still forested. Here you can find native wildlife, such as hippos, crocodiles, antelopes and elephants and giraffes. Birds are also omnipresent on the island and make the Rubondo Island national park an insider tip for ornithologists.
blocks.html: Rubondo Island national park sits on an island in the middle of Lake Victoria, the world's second largest lake. No one lives there, and 90% of the island remains covered in forest. Native wildlife includes hippos, crocodiles and antelopes, alongside elephants and giraffes. Birds are present in every corner of the island too, which makes Rubondo Island national park a well-kept secret among ornithologists.
